name: Ten Thousand Ripples
description: White Buddha heads emerge from the grass beside the lakefront path south of Diversey Harbor.
fact: Indira Johnson’s installation forms part of a citywide public-art project about peace and nonviolence.
practical: The Park District lists this as a temporary installation; view it from the surrounding paths.

name: Charitas
description: A bronze woman carrying two children stands just south of Theater on the Lake.
fact: Ida McClelland Stout designed it for the former children’s sanitarium in 1922. It returned to Lincoln Park in 2016.
practical: View the restored sculpture from the lakefront paths beside the theater.
coordinateSource: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1446941780; area-weighted centroid, checked inside the mapped feature; reviewed 2026-11-18

name: American Bison
description: A life-size steel bison stands near the entrance to the Peggy Notebaert Nature Museum.
fact: Chris Williams created the sculpture in 1999; it was installed here in 2012.
practical: Look for the outdoor sculpture near Cannon Drive; museum admission is separate.

name: North Avenue Beach Dunes
description: Native beach grasses form a narrow dune habitat beside the northern part of North Avenue Beach.
fact: About 13,000 marram-grass plants were added in 2018 to encourage dunes and reduce drifting sand.
practical: Enjoy the habitat from the adjacent paved trail and keep off the planted dunes.
coordinateSource: https://www.chicagoparkdistrict.com/parks-facilities/lincoln-park-north-ave-beach-dunes-natural-area; official Park District geolocation point, checked inside the mapped habitat polygon; reviewed 2026-11-18

name: The Butterfly House at Navy Pier
description: A seasonal walk-through butterfly habitat occupies Navy Pier’s north lawn.
fact: Visitors can observe free-flying butterflies in an enclosed garden.
practical: Closed for the season as of November 2026; the operator announces a return in 2027. Check reopening dates and admission before visiting.
coordinateSource: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1308482808; area-weighted centroid, checked inside the mapped feature; reviewed 2026-11-18

name: USS Chicago Anchor
description: A massive ship’s anchor rests near the eastern end of Navy Pier.
fact: The anchor came from the third USS Chicago and was installed here in 1995.
practical: Continue along the pier’s public promenade toward the east end.
coordinateSource: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1467696907; area-weighted centroid, checked inside the mapped feature; reviewed 2026-11-18

name: Bob Newhart Statue & Couch
description: A bronze Bob Newhart and an empty therapy couch invite a playful pause near the far end of Navy Pier.
fact: Studio EIS created the tribute to his television character, psychologist Bob Hartley.
practical: Find the sculpture near the pier’s southeast corner.
coordinateSource: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1467696911; area-weighted centroid, checked inside the mapped feature; reviewed 2026-11-18

name: Crack the Whip
description: Bronze children play a hand-in-hand running game near Navy Pier’s entrance.
fact: J. Seward Johnson Jr.’s sculpture was installed in 1996.
practical: Find it outside near the west end of the pier.

name: Chicago Harbor Lighthouse
description: A white lighthouse with red-roofed adjoining buildings stands on the offshore breakwater east of Navy Pier.
fact: Its conical tower dates to 1893; the lighthouse became a Chicago Landmark in 2003.
practical: An offshore sight, with no public land access. Look across the harbor from Navy Pier; this dot marks the lighthouse itself.
coordinateSource: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1188397898; area-weighted centroid, checked inside the mapped feature; reviewed 2026-11-18

name: U.S. Navy Submarine Memorial
description: A steel submarine-bulkhead memorial stands beside the Chicago River on the lower Riverwalk.
fact: It recalls 28 Wisconsin-built submarines that passed through Chicago on their way to World War II service.
practical: Follow the south-bank Riverwalk west from the lakefront, between Lake Shore Drive and Columbus Drive.

name: Riverwalk Gateway Murals
description: Painted ceramic panels fill the passage where the Chicago Riverwalk meets the Lakefront Trail beneath DuSable Lake Shore Drive.
fact: Ellen Lanyon’s 28 panels follow the river’s history through scenes of people, engineering and wildlife.
practical: The murals are at river level on the south bank, underneath the road bridge.
coordinateSource: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/751520450; area-weighted centroid, checked inside the mapped feature; reviewed 2026-11-18

name: Grant Park Fountain Figures
description: Four small bronze children inhabit their own circular fountains in the gardens north and south of Buckingham Fountain.
fact: Leonard Crunelle’s Crane Girl, Fisher Boy, Turtle Boy and Dove Girl moved to Grant Park in 1964.
practical: The map dot marks Fisher Boy in the northern pair. The other two fountains are south of Buckingham Fountain; water operates seasonally.
coordinateSource: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/230511525; area-weighted centroid, checked inside the mapped feature; point marks Fisher Boy in the northern pair, not the center of all four fountains; reviewed 2026-11-18

name: Aaron Montgomery Ward Bust
description: A bronze portrait honors the businessman whose lawsuits helped preserve Grant Park as open public space.
fact: Milton Horn’s bust was rededicated at this site in 2005.
practical: Look east of Michigan Avenue on the axis of 11th Street, at the southwest edge of Grant Park.

name: Burnham Centennial Prairie
description: Prairie grasses and wildflowers occupy a long stretch of the Burnham Wildlife Corridor south of McCormick Place.
fact: The Park District describes more than 50 acres of restored prairie habitat along this part of the lakefront.
practical: Explore from the paved Lakefront Trail or designated mulch paths. Natural areas are open dawn to dusk.
coordinateSource: https://www.chicagoparkdistrict.com/parks-facilities/burnham-wildlife-corridor-burnham-centennial-prairie; official Park District geolocation point, checked inside the mapped habitat polygon; reviewed 2026-11-18

name: Letter to Bessie Coleman
description: Tall steel poles carry cut-out symbols into the sky near Oakwood Beach.
fact: Bernard Williams created the work in 2018 in honor of aviation pioneer Bessie Coleman and her international spirit.
practical: Find the sculpture near the 39th Street lakefront, beside the trail north of Oakwood Beach.
coordinateSource: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1524460968; area-weighted centroid, checked inside the mapped feature; reviewed 2026-11-18

name: Sankofa for the Earth
description: An art-filled gathering space sits among the trees of the Burnham Wildlife Corridor.
fact: Artists from Bronzeville created the space around the Sankofa bird, a symbol of learning from the past.
practical: Use the signed woodland paths from the 47th Street access area. Stay on paths through the surrounding habitat.
